text:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime-streaming.p95/p99 spike detected in eu-prod cluster · SLO breach threshold crossed for 03:12 UTC · p95 -> 2.2s (baseline 450ms), p99 -> 8.6s (baseline 1.1s) · stream stall rate +18% · dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/streaming/eu-prod
ashwin (oncall): acked · joining bridge · posting runbook link https://runbooks.redwood/internal/triage/realtime-latency
maria (sre): quick notes: looks concentrated to streaming endpoints (route: /v1/stream/*) and EU region only. No large error rate spike, mostly timeouts and stalls. Quick metric snapshots: p95 2.2s, p99 8.6s, inflight requests 3x normal, kv_cache_miss_rate increased 4x.
leo (eng-runtime): checking logs for KV eviction bursts and large batch sizes. I see a KV eviction spike starting ~03:07 UTC on eu-az1 workers. Also some long GC pauses in worker logs. Sample PromQL I'm running: 
```
avg_over_time(stream_request_duration_seconds_p99[5m]) by (region)
rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m]) by (region)
```
ashwin (oncall): good — Maria, can you confirm if fallback model variants are healthy? If so we can route traffic to lower-latency variant while we investigate.
maria (sre): fallback variant (stream-v1-small) health = green for eu. p95 ~ 420ms. No warm-up issues. Prepared to shift. Also recommending temporary batch size reduction on runtime (batch_limit 16 -> 8) to avoid head-of-line stalls.
james (infra): infra check: eu GPU pool at 92% utilization on average; autoscaler had 3 pending nodes that didn't join due to k8s image pull slowness in eu-az1. I kicked a node recreate. If autoscaler can't add capacity we'll need to shift traffic off eu-az1.
ashwin (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) route 30% -> fallback stream-v1-small canary 2) reduce batch_limit to 8 in eu runtime 3) trigger worker rolling restart in problematic AZ 4) monitor p95/p99 and stall rate for 10m. I'll execute steps if no objections. :thumbsup:
leo (eng-runtime): I'll apply batch_limit change and start rolling restart of streaming-worker eu-az1 (will do one pod at a time). Command: 
```bash
redwood runtime update --region eu --service streaming-worker --set batch_limit=8 --rolling-restart
```
maria (sre): I'll flip canary routing: 
```bash
redwood router set-weight --route /v1/stream --variant stream-v1-small --weight 30% --region eu
```
Expect p95 to drop if KV eviction is root cause. I'll watch KV hit/miss and p95 in the canary group.
natalie (support): flagging customer impact: support ticket #INC-4129 from Acme corp reporting slow responses on chat attachments since ~03:05 UTC. I'm posting an update to the ticket now to say we're investigating and will update in 10m.
ashwin (oncall): assigning owners: maria -> routing/canary, leo -> runtime changes/roll restart, james -> infra node reprovision and k8s image pull root cause. Natalie -> customer comms. I'll coordinate and check back in 5m. If p99 remains >5s after canary we'll escalate to SEV.
maria (sre): canary at 30% applied. Initial canary metrics (1m): canary p95 460ms, baseline-prod eu p95 1.9s. KV miss rate in canary group is low. Looks promising.
leo (eng-runtime): rolling restart started, one pod restarted -> pod came back healthy in 45s. No crashloops. After first restart we saw small reduction in inflight tail latency.
james (infra): new node joined eu-az2 but az1 still missing due to registry timeout. Working with cloud team to re-publish image. If image pull doesn't succeed in 5m I'll force schedule to other AZ.
ashwin (oncall): monitoring dashboard now: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/streaming/eu-prod?var-canary=30% · set alert for p95 > 1.5s (auto-muted for canary group). Next check-in +5m.
incident-bot: ACTION: routing weight change executed by maria at 03:16:12 UTC · canary=30% -> stream-v1-small · batch_limit update queued by leo · rolling restart initiated · incident id: INC-2026
maria (sre): update at +4m: canary steady, canary p95 430ms, eu-prod overall p95 dropped to 980ms, p99 down to 3.1s. Stall rate trending down. Keeping canary at 30% while infra finishes.
natalie (support): updated Acme ticket and set customer notification: "We're actively mitigating a latency issue; temporary routing change applied; we'll follow up once stable."
nashwin (oncall): good progress. If p99 <2s and stall rate <5% in next 10m we'll close paging. If not, escalate to SEV and open bridge. For now keep monitoring; repo owners stand by. :eyes:
